Home.sub: One short diagnostic shows exactly which topics you know and which you don’t. Then Faroz turns each gap into a quest — practice, reading and a retest that proves progress.
Home.orbitLabel: Faroz logo at the centre with subjects orbiting around it
Home.howTitle: Your studies as a game loop: scan, spot, quest, retest.
Home.s1Body: A 25-minute diagnostic covers every topic. Answers save as you go.
Home.s2Body: Results by topic and by mistake pattern — the gap gets a name.
Home.s3Body: Weakest topic first: a short lesson, practice with instant feedback, one chapter.
Home.s4Body: New questions on the same topic. A later check shows if it stuck.
Home.p1Pattern: Pattern found in Arrays: expecting forEach and filter to return mapped values.
Home.q1: Lesson · map vs forEach vs filter
Home.p3Note: Retests use different questions, so improvement isn't memorised answers. A check two weeks later shows whether it stuck. Demo data.
Home.learnersTitle: Stop re-reading everything. Practise what you actually missed.
Home.learnersPhoto: a student studying at home with a laptop and notebook, warm natural light. Free license (Unsplash / Pexels).
Home.scanBody: One diagnostic per subject maps every topic.
Home.treeBody: See what's strong, what's next, what unlocks.
Home.xpNote: XP and streaks make practice stick — your real result always stays visible as a fraction.
Home.teachersTitle: See which question tripped the class — and why.
Home.teachersBody: Build a test in your language, assign it to a group, and see wrong answers grouped by misconception before the next lesson.
Home.why14: Treats forEach as returning an array
Home.why17: Expects push to return the array
Home.teachersPhoto: a young teacher helping students at laptops in a modern classroom. Free license (Unsplash / Pexels).
Home.centersBody: Spot a gap that repeats across groups and plan support where it's needed. Student-level detail stays with their teachers.
Home.centersNote: Arrays is below 55% in all three groups — a center-wide review topic. Demo center.
Home.centersPhoto: a small group of teenagers working together around one table at an education center. Free license.
Home.libraryTitle: Books picked for your gaps — many of them free.
Home.libraryNote: Real titles and editions. Covers are Faroz placeholders until publisher covers are loaded.
Home.pricingTitle: Free to learn. Paid to teach at scale.
Home.planLearnerBody: Diagnostics, quests, skill tree, XP and the library.
Home.planTeacherBody: Groups, test builder, question bank, class insights.
Home.planCenterBody: Many teachers and groups, center-wide analytics, roles.
Home.faq1q: Is it a game or real learning?
Home.faq1a: Real learning with a light game layer. XP and streaks keep you practising, but every result is shown as a plain fraction like 1 of 4.
Home.faq2q: How does Faroz know what I don’t know?
Home.faq2a: Every question is tagged with a topic and each wrong answer with a typical mistake. Results are grouped by those tags.
Home.faq3q: Does one test prove I’ve mastered a topic?
Home.faq3a: No. A topic is marked strong after a retest on new questions and a later check.
Home.faq4q: Can teachers use their own questions?
Home.faq4a: Yes — write them, reuse them from the bank, and publish in Tajik, Russian or English.
Home.faq5a: You and the teachers of your groups. Centers see group totals, not individual answers.
Home.endTitle: Start with one scan. Leave with a plan.
Home.endSub: Twenty questions, your topic map and your first quest — free.
